slides.title: IPv6  is the latest version of IP designed to replace IPv4
slides.body:
IPv6  is the latest version of IP designed to replace IPv4
IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses (~4.3 billion)
Which ran out as the number of internet devices grew
IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses (2¹²⁸)
Providing a huge number of unique addresses
It also improves routing, includes built-in security (IPsec), and supports automatic address configuration, removing the need for NAT
IPv6 - Internet Protocol Version 6

slides.title: Dual Stack
slides.body:
Dual Stack
A device runs both IPv4 and IPv6 simultaneously
It uses IPv6 when the destination supports it, IPv4 otherwise
No translation needed
Most modern operating systems (Windows, Linux, Android, iOS) are dual-stack by default
IPv4 vs IPv6 - Key Differences & Transition

slides.title: Tunneling
slides.body:
Tunneling
IPv6 packets are wrapped (encapsulated) inside IPv4 packets to cross IPv4-only networks
At the entry point: encapsulation
At the exit point: decapsulation
The IPv6 packet continues unchanged, examples: 6to4, ISATAP, Teredo

slides.body:
Translation (NAT64)
When an IPv6-only device must communicate with an IPv4-only device
A NAT64 gateway translates between the two protocols
DNS64 creates synthetic IPv6 addresses for IPv4-only destinations
